claim.pdf_says: where sharing-phrase is: SHARING WITH { ALL OTHER / NO OTHER / READ ONLY } — verified at 800 dpi: SHARING, ALL, NO, READ and ONLY carry underlines; WITH and BOTH occurrences of OTHER are printed without an underline and are therefore optional words.
claim.markdown_says: A fenced code block containing `⎧ ALL OTHER  ⎫` / `SHARING WITH    ⎨ NO OTHER   ⎬` / `⎩ READ ONLY  ⎭` — with no underlining and no figure note attached.
claim.why_it_matters: The OPEN general format directly above on the same page DOES carry a figure note recording its underlining ("OPEN, INPUT, OUTPUT, I-O, EXTEND, NO and REWIND are underlined in the printed figure (required words); WITH is not underlined (optional word)"), but that note scopes only to the OPEN figure and says nothing about the sharing-phrase. Without it the transcription makes OTHER look like a required word, so `OPEN INPUT F SHARING WITH ALL` and `SHARING WITH NO` — both legal — read as illegal, and `WITH` likewise reads as mandatory.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED by independent vector-geometry extraction and a 900 dpi pixel render; the claim is accurate as written. (1) OBJECTIVE EVIDENCE: the ISO PDF text layer is obfuscated, so I extracted the underline rules as vector drawings instead of trusting OCR. PDF page 705 carries exactly 24 drawing objects, all thin horizontal fills (h=0.47pt), forming 12 logical underlines (each is a 0.23pt leading stub plus the main run). Five of them fall in the sharing-phrase figure band (y 337-373): x 82.36-123.21 @ y=354.43 (w=40.85, 'SHARING', vertically centred on the 3-row brace); x 170.60-186.24 @ y=337.63 (w=15.64, row 1 'ALL'); x 170.60-182.50 @ y=355.13 (w=11.90, row 2 'NO'); x 170.60-194.64 @ y=372.41 (w=24.04, row 3 'READ'); x 200.94-224.52 @ y=372.41 (w=23.58, row 3 'ONLY'). There is NO rule anywhere to the right of x=123.21 on the SHARING row (so WITH is bare), none to the right of x=186.24 on row 1 (so the first OTHER is bare), and none to the right of x=182.50 on row 2 (so the second OTHER is bare). (2) METHOD VALIDATION: the same extraction over the OPEN figure above yields exactly seven underlines — OPEN, INPUT, OUTPUT, I-O, EXTEND, NO, REWIND — precisely the seven words the existing figure note enumerates, and no rule under WITH, which the note also states. The method therefore reproduces a known-good answer on the same page. (3) PIXEL CONFIRMATION: a 900 dpi clip of Rect(70,325,260,385) shows unmistakably that the rule under SHARING stops before WITH, that ALL and NO are underlined while the OTHER following each is not, and that READ and ONLY carry two separate rules. (4) THE NOTATION MATTERS: ISO/IEC 1989:2023 §8.3.2.4.3 states 'Within each format, uppercase words that are not underlined are called optional words and may be specified at the user's option with no effect on the semantics of the format' (see also §5.2.3). So WITH and OTHER are omissible and `SHARING ALL`, `SHARING WITH ALL`, `SHARING NO`, `SHARING WITH NO` are all legal, while READ ONLY requires both words. Stripping the underlining inverts this: every word reads as required. (5) MARKDOWN CONFIRMED DEFICIENT: specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 28837-28841 hold the fenced sharing-phrase block; line 28843 is 'where retry-phrase is described in 14.7.9, RETRY phrase'. No figure note intervenes. The only note on the page is at line 28833, explicitly headed '**Figure notes (14.9.27.2, OPEN):**' and enumerating only the OPEN figure's words — it does not scope to the sharing-phrase, exactly as the claim states. (6) INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY CLINCHES IT: this transcription records this very underlining at three other sites for the identical syntax — line 15613 (SHARING clause §12.4.5.15): '`SHARING`, `ALL`, `NO`, `READ`, and `ONLY` are underlined in the printed standard (required words). `WITH` and `OTHER` are **not** underlined — they are optional words'; line 14876 (SELECT Format 3); and lines 14770/14812 (SELECT Formats 1 and 2, both listing OTHER and WITH among the non-underlined). Attaching underline-recording figure notes is this transcription's established convention (dozens of them exist), so the omission at §14.9.27.2 is a genuine, isolated lapse rather than a uniform stylistic choice — and it disagrees with what the same document says about the same words elsewhere. I looked for every ground to refute: the text is not reflowed or present on an adjacent line, this is not page-break furniture or wrapping, neither source is misquoted, and the difference plainly changes what source text the format admits. None of the refutation grounds apply.
verdict.corrected_description: Accurate as filed; only one immaterial correction. The claim says the underlining was 'verified at 800 dpi' — I verified it at 900 dpi and, more decisively, by extracting the underline rules as PDF vector geometry (the page's 24 drawing objects), which removes any reliance on visual judgement. The substance is exactly right: in the §14.9.27.2 sharing-phrase figure the printed rules cover SHARING, ALL, NO, READ and ONLY, while WITH and both occurrences of OTHER are printed bare. FIX: append a figure note after the closing fence at specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 28841, worded to match the existing sibling note at line 28613/15613 — e.g. '> **Figure notes (14.9.27.2, sharing-phrase):** `SHARING`, `ALL`, `NO`, `READ`, and `ONLY` are underlined in the printed figure (required words). `WITH` and both occurrences of `OTHER` are **not** underlined — they are optional words. The braces are a plain required choice: exactly one of the three alternatives shall be selected. No choice indicators appear in this figure.' Two consequences worth carrying into the compiler: `SHARING [WITH] ALL [OTHER]`, `SHARING [WITH] NO [OTHER]` and `SHARING [WITH] READ ONLY` must all parse (OTHER and WITH optional in every combination), and READ ONLY must require BOTH words since both are underlined. Note also that the OPEN figure note at line 28833 is itself correct and complete for the OPEN figure — the defect is solely the absent note on the subordinate sharing-phrase figure, not an error in the existing one.
